title: Hosted API demo - Chat/Text generation basics (Petal Analytics)
summary: Intro demo of Redwood Hosted API focused on chat/text generation: streaming, tuning params (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), retry behavior, idempotency keys, and Console + Optimize recommendations. Customer interested in latency and cost tradeoffs; asked about SOC2/KMS and VPC/Dedicated options. Agreed next steps: share security pack, pricing, schedule a short benchmark with sample prompts.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-01 11:00am PT / Duration: ~48 minutes / Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lina (Redwood SE), Raj (Head Eng), Olivia (ML Eng), Marta (CTO), Daniel (Security)

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Samir, AE on the account, and Lina will run the technical demo. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Raj (Petal): Good, thanks. Excited to see the hosted API flow. we evaluated a few vendors so curious about latency and cost.
[00:12] Lina (Redwood): awesome. Goal today: show chat/text generation basics — streaming, key params, retries, then a quick Console and Optimize view. we'll keep it practical.
[00:20] Marta (Petal): that works. we'll focus on realtime chat use-case for our ops dashboard, plus some batch summarization for reports.

[00:35] Lina: starting with the API — here's a simple chat request. you can stream tokens over SSE or websockets, so the UI gets partial tokens immediately. note: streaming reduces perceived latency but doesn't change total compute cost.
[00:50] Olivia (Petal): streaming — do you send intermediate deltas or full messages? we're worried about flicker and re-assembly.
[00:57] Lina: good q. SDKs give you chunk framing; typical pattern is append token deltas and render progressively. we also provide heuristics to avoid tiny-chunk spam — buffer for 40-60ms if needed.
[01:12] Raj: and how about reconnection? if we drop mid-stream, can we resume?
[01:18] Lina: we don't have byte-level resume today. pattern is to use idempotency keys on the request, and the server can return the final output if you retry with the same key. for streaming reconnects we recommend saving partial client state and either re-requesting with the same key or fall back to a second request with a short history.

[01:35] Samir: quick interjection — on retries, Redwood supports exponential backoff and jitter. we expose retry guidance in the SDKs and sample code in the Console. Lina, show param tuning.
[01:44] Lina: sure. typical generation params: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences, presence/ frequency penalties. small changes in temp (0.0-0.4 vs 0.6-1.0) change determinism. for customer UX we'd suggest 0.2-0.6 for concise outputs.
[02:05] Olivia: do you have any automatic fallback model variants for cost vs latency?
[02:10] Lina: yes — routing policies can fallback to cheaper quantized variants automatically if capacity's tight. Console lets you set policies by latency SLO or cost target.

[02:25] Raj: can you explain batching/caching? our throughput is spiky during incidents.
[02:30] Lina: Redwood does continuous batching in the runtime to improve throughput; for chat we also provide prefix caching (KV cache) so repeated system prompts or long context prefixes don't get recomputed. Optimize will suggest batching windows and cache TTLs based on your payload distribution.

[02:50] Marta: security questions — we need SOC2 docs, audit logs, and KMS integration. also does hosted retain customer prompts?
[02:58] Samir: we maintain SOC2 and ISO artifacts; we can share the security pack. Hosted retains request logs for X days by default (configurable). for encrypted-at-rest keys, we integrate with customer KMS or HSM. if you'll need total control, there's Redwood Private for VPC or on-prem.
[03:15] Daniel (Petal): we might need log redaction or retention shorter than 30 days.
[03:19] Samir: that's configurable. we can set retention policies and audit log levels per account; Lina will follow up with the exact options.

[03:33] Lina: shifting back to the demo — quick Console tour: route creation, model selection, and traffic split for canary. here's the latency dashboard per route and per-token cost breakdown. you can also pin model versions for stable rollouts.
[03:50] Olivia: can we see per-user quotas and rate limiting?
[03:55] Lina: yep. Console shows per-key quotas, per-route rate limits, and burst windows. we also show recent throttles and suggestions to tune concurrency.

[04:10] Raj: about retries — we saw retries leading to duplicate side-effects in our current flow. do you support idempotency or request dedupe?
[04:18] Lina: yes. use an idempotency key header — the platform dedups identical generation requests. for actions triggered by responses (e.g., create-ticket), we recommend the app layer also dedupe using a request id, but the idempotency header reduces double billing and duplicate model calls.

[04:35] Samir: on observability — we provide token-level cost breakdowns and trace IDs you can ingest into your APM. Optimize also flags regressions if eval prompts degrade.
[04:46] Olivia: Eval prompts — can we run our QA prompt set automatically on new model versions?
[04:50] Lina: yes, Console has eval hooks and you can set regression thresholds to block rollouts.

[05:02] Raj: curious about cold-starts and p99 latency. do you keep warm pools?
[05:07] Lina: Hosted keeps warm pools at regional scale; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with tighter p99. cold starts for large models are mitigated with prefueling and KV cache warmup. we can run a small benchmark to show median and p90/p99 numbers for your prompt mix.

[05:26] Marta: cost question — how granular is pricing? per-token only or model-specific multipliers?
[05:31] Samir: pricing is per-token with model tiers and optional dedicated capacity. we'll share the rate card. Optimize suggestions can show dollar impact of batching and quantization changes.

[05:45] Lina: quick demo scenario: we'll do a short live call using the SDK to generate a 3-turn chat. i'll use streaming mode so you can see incremental tokens. (typing noises)
[05:58] [06:00] Lina: "system: You are a helpful assistant. user: summarize incident logs into a short report." sending request now...
[06:12] [06:15] Lina: partial stream: "Summary: At 03:14 UTC an error cascade..." (lina laughs) transcript shows small tokenization quirk but overall clean.
[06:28] Olivia: that streaming looks smooth. what's the typical payload size and tokenization behavior for log text?
[06:35] Lina: logs tokenize compactly; CPU cost for tokenization is small relative to model runtime but we account for it. for long logs, we recommend chunking and summarizing incrementally or using a sliding window to keep context within max tokens.

[06:50] Raj: about SDKs — we use Typescript and Python. do you support server-side streaming and browser streaming securely?
[06:56] Lina: yes. both SDKs support streaming; for browser we recommend proxying via a backend to keep keys safe or using short-lived keys via the Console. we also support signed ephemeral tokens.

[07:12] Daniel: any limitations on PII in hosted? we need to prove data isn't used for training.
[07:18] Samir: Redwood Hosted can be configured to not use customer data for training; we'll include statement in the security pack. Private deployments give the strictest controls.

[07:30] Lina: last piece — retry knobs. SDK default: 3 retries with exponential backoff starting at 200ms with jitter. we expose these values. we also expose a per-route circuit breaker to avoid thrashing.
[07:45] Raj: what about rate-limits during incidents — do you have burst capacity?
[07:49] Samir: Hosted has burst options and Dedicated gives predictable reserved throughput; you can configure autoscaling policies and burst credits in the Console.

[08:00] Marta: okay great. let's talk timeline — we want a quick POC next two weeks and then evaluate Dedicated if results look good.
[08:06] Samir: sounds good. Lina — benchmarks and quickstart?
[08:09] Lina: i'll send a benchmark script and a small sample app. we can run the POC on Hosted and capture p50/p90/p99 and cost per 1k requests.

[08:20] Raj: any gotchas we should know for prompt engineering and param defaults?
[08:24] Lina: defaults are conservative: temperature 0.2, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 512. for extractive summaries set temperature near 0.0. also validate stop sequences to avoid over-generation. Optimize will suggest param sweeps if you want automated tuning.

[08:40] Samir: recap and next steps: we'll share security pack, pricing, and benchmark artifacts. Petal to share prompt set and traffic profile. schedule the benchmark call next week.
[08:50] Marta: thanks all — this was helpful.
[08:54] Raj: thanks, speak soon.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., "prefueling" heard as "pre-fooling" in one clip), speaker attribution mostly correct but a couple lines labeled generically in the raw export. Links shared: security pack (link), quickstart repo (github.com/redwood/quickstart), benchmark script (gists/benchmark-ptl).
